verses.text: “Flee for safety, you children of Benjamin, out of the middle of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise up a signal on Beth Haccherem; for evil looks out from the north, and a great destruction.
I will cut off the comely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion.
Shepherds with their flocks shall come to her; they shall pitch their tents against her all around; they shall feed everyone in his place.”
“Prepare war against her; arise, and let us go up at noon. Woe to us! For the day declines, for the shadows of the evening are stretched out.
Arise, and let us go up by night, and let us destroy her palaces.”
For Yahweh of Armies said, “Cut down trees, and cast up a mound against Jerusalem: this is the city to be visited; she is wholly oppression within her.
As a well produces its waters, so she produces her wickedness: violence and destruction is heard in her; before me continually is sickness and wounds.
Be instructed, Jerusalem, lest my soul be alienated from you; lest I make you a desolation, a land not inhabited.”
Yahweh of Armies says, “They shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine. Turn again your hand as a grape gatherer into the baskets.”
To whom shall I speak and testify, that they may hear? Behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they can’t listen. Behold, Yahweh’s word has become a reproach to them. They have no delight in it.

Therefore I am full of Yahweh’s wrath. I am weary with holding in. “Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the assembly of young men together; for even the husband with the wife shall be taken, the aged with him who is full of days.
Their houses shall be turned to others, their fields and their wives together; for I will stretch out my hand on the inhabitants of the land, says Yahweh.”
“For from their least even to their greatest, everyone is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even to the priest, everyone deals falsely.
They have healed also the hurt of my people superficially, saying, ‘Peace, peace!’ when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall; at the time that I visit them, they shall be cast down,” says Yahweh.
Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
I set watchmen over you, saying, ‘Listen to the sound of the trumpet!’ But they said, ‘We will not listen!’
Therefore hear, you nations, and know, congregation, what is among them.
Hear, earth! Behold, I will bring evil on this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not listened to my words; and as for my law, they have rejected it.
To what purpose comes there to me frankincense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices pleasing to me.”
Therefore Yahweh says, “Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people. The fathers and the sons together shall stumble against them. The neighbor and his friend shall perish.”
Yahweh says, “Behold, a people comes from the north country. A great nation shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth.

They take hold of bow and spear. They are cruel, and have no mercy. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a man to the battle, against you, daughter of Zion.”
We have heard its report; our hands become feeble: anguish has taken hold of us, and pains as of a woman in labor.
Don’t go out into the field, nor walk by the way; for the sword of the enemy and terror, are on every side.
Daughter of my people, clothe yourself with sackcloth, and wallow in ashes! Mourn, as for an only son, most bitter lamentation; for the destroyer shall suddenly come on us.
“I have made you a tester of metals and a fortress among my people; that you may know and try their way.
They are all grievous rebels, going about with slanders; they are brass and iron: they all of them deal corruptly.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed of the fire: in vain do they go on refining; for the wicked are not plucked away.
Men will call them rejected silver, because Yahweh has rejected them.”

footnotes.content: The trumpet call, the signal fire—urgency born from love. God warns His people first through His watchmen before judgment comes. Even now, He gives us time to turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zion, once lovely and cherished, now marked for loss. The Lord grieves what His own hands must prune away—not cruelty, but the only remedy for a heart turned wholly to itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shepherds and their flocks encircle the city to lay siege. What once was a place of gathering becomes surrounded, cut off—the shape that God's judgment takes when rebellion hardens into stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The enemy generals urge haste at noon. Even the invaders feel time pressing, shadows growing long. How telling: urgency fills both the pursuer and the pursued.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By night they come to tear down what took lifetimes to build. Palaces that sheltered pride fall dark and empty. The Lord who gives also takes away—and His name stays blessed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command to fell trees for siege mounds is specific, practical—the Lord's judgment uses real weapons and real siege craft. Nothing fantastical here, only the natural fruit of rebellion allowed to ripen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A well that yields poison instead of water, a city that springs forth oppression as naturally as water flows. This is what we become when we train ourselves to thirst for the wrong things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even in the shadow of judgment, God calls Jerusalem to learn. His heart would turn from wrath if the city would turn toward Him. The door remains ajar, though time grows short.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Like a grape picker gleaning every last vine, the judgment will be thorough—nothing is hidden from His eye. Yet even here is mercy's image: the gatherer's hand, the basket ready, the care of one who notices.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their ears are uncircumcised—stubborn, closed from the inside. They have rejected the word until it became a joke to them. How tragic when we laugh at the very thing meant to save us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet can barely hold back God's wrath—he is full of it, worn out by restraint. The Lord's patience is real, and so is His sorrow when it must end. There is nothing casual about this judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fields, houses, wives—all that a person builds and cherishes will pass to strangers. The hand of God stretches out over all the land. Only what is held loosely survives the grip of judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From least to greatest, all reach for gain; prophets and priests alike have forgotten whom they serve. When the shepherds become wolves, the flock has nowhere left to turn—except to the Shepherd beyond them all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace, peace—the comfortable lie that heals wounds in name only. False prophets soothe the conscience while the real sickness deepens. Better an honest wound than an infected band-aid.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No shame, no blushing—the conscience so seared that even abomination feels normal. When a people can no longer blush, judgment has already won. The heart hardens before the city falls.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stand in the ways, ask for the old paths, walk in them—the Lord offers an ancient road to rest for the soul. But they refuse. Even wisdom plainly offered is worthless if the ear won't hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Watchmen set on the walls, trumpets sounding—every warning given. But 'We will not listen' becomes their refrain, each time harder to say, until it becomes the truth of who they are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations and congregations are called to witness. What unfolds in Jerusalem becomes a lesson to the world—the wages of rejecting the Lord written in ash and exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The earth itself hears the judgment because the people would not. Evil comes as the fruit of their own thoughts ripened on the vine of their refusal. God did not speak in darkness but in the light of day.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Frankincense from Sheba, sweet cane from afar—costly gifts laid on the altar, yet the Lord turns His face away. Offerings mean nothing when the heart is far from Him. The ritual has become a mask.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stumbling blocks laid in their path, fathers and sons falling together, neighbors perishing in company. Even in judgment, the relationships are real—the loss is relational, not abstract.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A people rising from the north—Babylon, the instrument of God's wrath. What seems like mere military conquest is the hand of the Lord set in motion by the hardened hearts of His own people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bow and spear, cruelty and mercilessness—the destroyers come with all the marks of human warfare. Yet through it all, the Lord is working. Even the nations that know Him not serve His purposes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The report has come; hands grow weak; labor pains grip the soul. Fear teaches what words could not—that the Lord's warning was true, and the cost of ignoring it is written now in trembling flesh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terror on every side, no safety in the field or road. When judgment falls, there is nowhere to hide but in the shelter that the Lord Himself provides—and most never think to look there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sackcloth and ashes, mourning as for an only son—this is real grief, not theatrical. The destroyer comes suddenly, and a people who refused the gentle hand of their Father now face His hand stretched out in judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah himself becomes a tester of metals, a fortress among the people—called to discern what is true and what is dross, to stand firm when all around him crumbles. The prophet's own refining is his calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grievous rebels spreading slander, hardened as brass and iron. When people stop being malleable before the Lord's hands, they become instruments of their own destruction—unbendable, unredeemable in their chosen stubbornness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bellows blow, the fire burns hot, yet the wicked remain—the refining fire cannot extract good from those who refuse to yield. Some metal is too corrupted for purification; it must be cast away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rejected silver—a name that echoes through the centuries for any who harden their hearts against the Lord's call. Yet the very word 'rejected' reminds us that acceptance was always possible. Today, the smelter's work continues; some are still being refined.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
